q: How do FHRPs differ from SSO?

o.A: FHRPs use OTV for redundancy, and SSO uses VXLAN for state synchronization.
o.B: FHRPs provide gateway redundancy, and SSO provides failover within a single device.
o.C: FHRPs influence bandwidth allocation, and SSO influences routing decisions.
o.D: FHRPs maintain state information within a single device, and SSO manages state information across multiple devices.

e: FHRPs (First Hop Redundancy Protocols like HSRP, VRRP, GLBP) provide gateway redundancy by allowing multiple routers to present a single virtual default gateway to hosts, ensuring continued connectivity if one router fails. SSO (Stateful Switchover) enables failover within a single device, particularly between the active and standby supervisor modules in modular switches or routers, preserving forwarding and control plane state during a switchover.

e: In a Cisco SD-Access wireless architecture, the fabric control plane node (also known as the LISP map-server/map-resolver) is responsible for maintaining the endpoint ID (EID) database. It maps endpoint IDs (e.g., IP or MAC addresses) to RLOCs (Routing Locators) used within the SD-Access fabric.

q: Which WLC discovery method uses CISCO-CAPWAP-CONTROLLER as an identifier?

o.B: DHCP
o.C: L3 broadcast
o.D: DNS

e: In the DNS-based WLC discovery method, the AP performs a DNS lookup for the name CISCO-CAPWAP-CONTROLLER. The DNS server responds with the IP address of the controller, allowing the AP to discover and join it. Other methods (like static, DHCP option 43, or L3 broadcast) use different mechanisms and do not rely on that specific DNS name.

q: In a Cisco SD-Access solution, which device connects wired endpoints to the fabric?

o.B: fabric border node
o.C: intermediate node
o.D: control plane node

e: In Cisco SD-Access, the fabric edge node is the switch that directly connects to wired endpoints (hosts, PCs, IP phones). It acts as the entry point into the fabric, handling encapsulation/decapsulation of VXLAN traffic and mapping endpoints into the virtualized network.

q: Which network design principle should be followed to improve Layer 2 stability in an enterprise campus design?

o.A: Extend all user VLANs throughout the access layer.
o.B: Extend all user VLANs throughout the core layer.
o.C: Extend only required user VLANs throughout the access layer.
o.D: Extend only required user VLANs throughout the aggregation layer.

e: To improve Layer 2 stability in a campus design, VLANs should be kept local and extended only where needed. Extending unnecessary VLANs increases the size of the broadcast domain and risk of spanning-tree instability. Limiting VLANs to the access layer where they are required reduces failure domains and enhances network stability.

q: Which two Cisco SD-Access components provide communication between traditional network elements and the controller layer? (Choose two.)

o.B: partner ecosystem
o.C: network control platform
o.D: fabric overlay

e: In Cisco SD-Access, the network underlay provides IP connectivity and transports control/management traffic between devices and the controller layer. The fabric overlay (VXLAN-based) enables communication between the controller layer and the fabric-enabled nodes, supporting policy and segmentation across the fabric. Together, they bridge traditional network elements with the SD-Access control functions.

q: When an endpoint moves in a LISP-enabled topology, which part of the distributed mapping database record stays the same?

o.B: map server
o.C: RLOC
o.D: Map-Resolver

e: In LISP, the Endpoint Identifier (EID) represents the identity of the endpoint and does not change when the device moves. The Routing Locator (RLOC) changes based on the device's new location, while the EID remains constant in the distributed mapping database.

q: Which two components are part of the Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN solution? (Choose two.)

o.B: border node
o.C: Cisco Prime
o.D: fabric edge node

e: The Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN solution includes vBond as the orchestration component for device authentication and control-plane connectivity, and cEdge as the WAN edge device that forwards traffic and participates in the SD-WAN fabric.

q: How does Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN facilitate multicloud IaaS access to cloud providers such as Microsoft Azure, AWS, and Google Cloud?

o.A: by use of NBAR for automation of best path selection into the cloud providers
o.B: by creation of IPsec connectivity to cloud colocations
o.C: by creation of BGP peerings to individual cloud providers
o.D: by extension of the SD-WAN fabric into the cloud providers

e: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN enables multicloud access by extending the SD-WAN fabric into cloud environments using virtual WAN edge devices, allowing seamless and policy-driven connectivity across on-premises and cloud resources.
